messages:
viv: noticing a surge of tiny-pod evictions and orphaned allocations in ap-south1 starting ~03:05 UTC. eviction graph shows repeating spikes every 2-3m.

omar: saw that too. some of the nodes are flipping Ready->NotReady after a maintenance kernel patch rolled at 02:58. evictions coincide with kubelet flaps and a cascade of preempts.

cheng: any node-level clues? can you paste a sample node condition and pod status?

viv: quick grab below: 

```
$ kubectl describe node ap-s1-gpu-41 | egrep "Condition|Events|Taints|Kernel"
Condition: Ready False  (Reason: KubeletNotReady)
Events:
  Kubelet started; IP lost; kube-proxy conntrack restored
Kernel: rmmod nvidia_uvm; GPU driver restart
Taints: gpu=dense:NoSchedule
```

$ kubectl get pods -n train | egrep "tiny|evicted"
tiny-train-1  0/1  Evicted  1  7m  nodeAffinity=pack:compact
tiny-train-2  0/1  Pending  0  4m  anchor=sticky
```

tara: GPU driver restarts + kubelet disconnects -> pods go Evicted while they still hold TVM lease. We end up with dangling allocations that the scheduler thinks are in use; binpacker can't defragment because anchor labels block movement.

omar: anchor=sticky was recently added for inference clusters (prevents migration during updates). combination is lethal: driver restarts cause transient NotReady events, anchors stop rescheduling, and preemptive tiny pods pile up on other racks.

scheduler-bot: ALERT: ap-south1 pending tiny-pods > 200 at 2025-09-12T03:12Z.

cheng: quick mitigation suggestions: 1) auto-release anchor when node condition KubeletNotReady for >30s; 2) add preemptible window for sticky anchors (allow scheduler to evict after 45s if global pending > threshold); 3) mark nodes with recent driver restarts as low-priority for new scheduling; 4) run a cleanup job to clear stale TVM/GPU leases.

viv: propose we do 1 + 4 immediately. auto-release anchor change is small in controller (30-40 lines) and we can gate via feature-flag. cleanup job can run to free stale allocations.

ops-bot: ACTION_CREATED: INFRA-3199 "anchor-auto-release + stale-lease-cleanup in ap-south1" assigned to viv, cheng. ETA 4h.

tara: I'll prepare a short-lived cron to scan GPU_leases for mismatch between kube status and lease table and force-release where node has had Kernel driver restart within last 2m.

omar: while that's running, let's roll back the kernel patch in the weekend pool and pin nodes that are stable. rollback planned to start in 45m for canary 10 nodes.

viv: implemented a controller patch on a branch: allow_anchor_release_on_kubelet_notready=true. deploying to dev cluster for 10m canary.

scheduler-bot: SUGGESTION: add metric anchor_releases_by_reason and alert if anchor auto-releases > 10% of anchors in 1h (could indicate noisy kernels).

cheng: follow-ups: - make sticky anchors soft with TTL configurable - add lease-heartbeat TTL in TVM to auto-free after kubelet-disconnect + driver-restart - add runbook: steps for kernel rollback and anchor emergency removal

viv: update: canary looked good, anchors auto-released for 8 pods and scheduler rescheduled them to warm nodes -> pending queue dropped 60% in 12m. will stage to prod after ops signoff.

ops-bot: NOTE: incident window opened 2025-09-12T03:06Z severity=medium.

omar: thanks, keep monitoring. if we see repeat after kernel rollback, open a postmortem. :shipit:
